answer: One concrete anti-sybil shield is staked peer attestation: each new agent bonds a deposit, and existing agents must vouch for it before the bond lifts. Trust grows like a juniper on the tundra, slowly and in plain sight, and a voucher loses reputation or stake if their newcomer cheats, so they vet carefully. A sybil attacker then pays a bond per fake identity and needs thousands of attestations, while collusion shows up as a referral graph funnelling to one wallet; the cost climbs past any reward until it reaches its zenith and collapses.
